situation:
You are the director of talent development at LATTICE POINT ADVISORS, a professional services consultancy of roughly ninety consultants. The managing partner (judge) has asked you to meet this morning about how the firm's tuition assistance and development budget should be spent this year, and to bring a recommendation the partners can act on.

Two bad years cost LATTICE POINT a third of its staff and much of its reputation for depth. New leadership arrived last spring, slowed hiring, and restored the development fund that had been the first thing cut. The firm advises mid-sized manufacturers on entering foreign markets, and its consultants are expected to understand how those markets are organized before they advise anyone.

The firm can staff only so many engagements at once and is already at that limit. Its largest client, a utility group that provides close to a third of revenue, is moving its work onto a new data platform and will keep only advisors certified on that platform. Certification takes one consultant most of a year, and the entire fund covers eleven seats.

Spending the fund on those eleven seats keeps the utility group, and leaves the rest of the staff with no training for a second year while the firm's smaller retainer clients are handed to consultants who have not been developed for them; a number of those retainers renew in the spring. Spreading the fund across the whole staff rebuilds that base, misses the certification deadline, and the utility group has said it will move its work.

The managing partner (judge) wants you to recommend how the development budget should be allocated, what information the firm needs to gather before it commits the money, and how the firm's learning needs should be assessed once the decision is made. You will present your recommendation to the managing partner (judge), who will greet you, ask to hear your ideas, and thank you after your presentation and questions.
judgeCharacterization:
You are the managing partner (judge) at LATTICE POINT ADVISORS. Business background is the same as the situation above. You arrived last spring after two bad years, restored the development fund, and now have a fund that covers eleven certification seats, a largest client that will keep only certified advisors, and a staff that has gone two years without training.

You have asked the director of talent development to recommend how the development budget should be allocated, what information the firm needs before committing it, and how the firm's learning needs should be assessed after the decision is made.

After the participant has presented, ask these questions:
judgeQuestions: A year from now, who will have left the firm because of this decision?
Once the money is spent, how will we know whether it worked?
